stories.headline: Iran hits US base in Jordan; US and Saudi Arabia strike militias in Iraq as oil jumps

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said Iran launched a missile barrage at US forces in the Middle East at 17:45 EDT on Tuesday, July 28 (21:45 GMT), calling it an 'attempted surprise attack'; all missiles were intercepted.
key_facts.excerpt: The US said the Iranian attack occurred at 17:45 EDT (21:45 GMT) on Tuesday, with all missiles 'successfully intercepted'.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it targeted a US air base and a command centre in Jordan, and that its naval forces struck three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz after they 'ignored warnings'.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC said it had targeted a US air base and a command centre in Jordan ... It also said that naval forces had struck three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz after they 'ignored warnings'.

key_facts.fact: Hours later, US and Saudi forces struck Iran-aligned militia sites across eastern Iraq; Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces said at least 20 of its members were killed and 32 wounded in strikes on bases in Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala and Diyala.
key_facts.excerpt: The PMF said in a statement on Wednesday morning that at least 20 of its fighters had been killed and 32 others wounded in US-Saudi strikes on a number of its headquarters.

key_facts.fact: Centcom said the joint strikes hit 'multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq' in response to more than 30 IRGC-directed drone attacks in the previous 72 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: Centcom said the joint US-Saudi strikes hit 'multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq in a strong response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours.'

key_facts.fact: Trump told Fox News on Wednesday that US forces would be 'hitting them hard', adding 'they're going to get a beating'; the attack came a day after he met Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House, and at least 18 American soldiers have been killed since the war began in February.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We'll be hitting them hard,' Yingst quoted the president as saying. 'They're going to get a beating.' ... At least 18 American soldiers have been killed since the war began in February.

key_facts.fact: Oil prices jumped more than 4% in early Wednesday trading, with Brent up $3.71 to $85.79 a barrel and US crude up $3.78 to $83.04, after Jordan's air defences intercepted five Iranian missiles early Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude, the international standard, jumped $3.71 to $85.79 a barrel. Benchmark U.S. crude gained $3.78 to $83.04 a barrel. ... Jordan's air defenses intercepted five missiles launched from Iran early Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: About 20% of the world's traded oil normally flows through the Strait of Hormuz, the focus of weeks of escalation before a roughly three-day lull was broken.
key_facts.excerpt: The calm persisted for about three days following weeks of escalation over the strategic Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf waterway and narrow chokepoint through which 20% of the world's traded oil normally flows.

stories.headline: Japan quake death toll hits 18 as rescuers dig through collapsed mall and paper factory

key_facts.fact: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck the Kumamoto area of Kyushu at 16:27 local time on Tuesday (07:27 GMT), with a shallow epicentre 10 km deep about 20 km south of Kumamoto city; the USGS later put the magnitude at 6.8.
key_facts.excerpt: Tuesday's quake hit the Kumamoto prefecture on Kyushu island at 16:27 local time (07:27 GMT). ... The JMA measured the earthquake magnitude at 7.1 and the US Geological Survey later placed it at 6.8.

key_facts.fact: By Wednesday the confirmed death toll had reached at least 18, including a foreigner, with at least 62 people injured, six seriously, according to the Kumamoto prefectural government.
key_facts.excerpt: a powerful earthquake that killed at least 18 people, including a foreigner, in southwestern Japan ... also left at least 62 people injured, six of them seriously, the prefectural government said.

key_facts.fact: At the Aeon Mall in Kashima, about 3,000 customers were evacuated to a parking lot before a gas explosion tore through another part of the mall; the second floor collapsed, four deaths were confirmed at the site and three people remained missing, Aeon president Akio Yoshida said.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said some 3,000 customers were evacuated to a parking lot before a gas explosion happened in another part of the mall ... Three people remained missing, while four deaths were confirmed at the mall site, according to Aeon President Akio Yoshida.

key_facts.fact: A chimney collapse at a Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro killed five people, with seven rescued and four still believed trapped.
key_facts.excerpt: In nearby Yatsushino, a chimney collapse at a Nippon Paper Industries factory killed five people while seven others were rescued from the debris.

key_facts.fact: Kyushu has recorded more than 100 aftershocks, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called the rescue effort 'truly a race against time', saying more than 4,600 personnel had been deployed while temperatures hit about 35C.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's south-western Kyushu region has had more than 100 aftershocks ... Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi warned it was 'truly a race against time' ... More than 4,600 personnel were deployed to help with rescue efforts.

key_facts.fact: The Japan Meteorological Agency warned residents to expect possible further quakes of up to maximum seismic intensity 7 over the following two to three days.
key_facts.excerpt: 'For the next week or so, especially the next two to three days, we would like people to watch out for potential earthquakes with a maximum seismic intensity of 7,' a JMA official said.

sources.title: Rescuers search for survivors after a 7.1 quake kills 18 in southwestern Japan
More than 100 aftershocks hit Japan after powerful quake that killed 13

stories.headline: Russia's FSB charges Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorism, issues arrest warrant

key_facts.fact: Russia's FSB announced on Wednesday, July 29, that it had charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity and issued an international arrest warrant for him.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's FSB security service announced Wednesday that it had issued a warrant for the arrest of Telegram founder Pavel Durov on charges of facilitating terrorist activities.

key_facts.fact: The FSB said Telegram had been used 'to prepare and co-ordinate acts of sabotage and terror' inside Russia and had failed to remove channels, chats and bots used by Ukrainian secret services.
key_facts.excerpt: The FSB ... said Telegram had been used 'to prepare and co-ordinate acts of sabotage and terror' inside Russia and had failed to remove channels, chats and bots used by Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: The charge of aiding terrorist activity carries a maximum sentence of 15 years in prison in Russia.
key_facts.excerpt: The charge of aiding terrorist activities carries a maximum prison sentence of 15 years in prison.

key_facts.fact: Telegram's official X account responded to the charge by posting an image of Durov raising his middle finger.
key_facts.excerpt: Shortly after the charge was announced, Telegram's account on X posted an image showing Durov holding up his middle finger.

key_facts.fact: Durov, 41, left Russia in 2014 after refusing to shut down opposition communities on VKontakte, lives in Dubai and holds French and UAE citizenship; Telegram has around 950 million users worldwide and roughly 90 million in Russia, where Roskomnadzor has been throttling the app.
key_facts.excerpt: Multi-billionaire Durov, 41, has lived outside of Russia for many years and holds French and United Arab Emirates (UAE) passports. ... Telegram is used by around 950 million people worldwide.

key_facts.fact: Telegram has around 90 million users in Russia and has become hard to use without a VPN as Roskomnadzor slows downloads and blocks video and voice calls.
key_facts.excerpt: Telegram, which has around 90 million users in Russia, has become difficult to use without a virtual private network, or VPN, as the state media regulator Roskomnadzor slows download speeds and blocks video and voice calls on the platform.

key_facts.fact: The FSB said Ukrainian intelligence officers posed as women on Telegram's 'Daivinchik' dating service to recruit young Russians, and that 46 users of the service had been detained across 16 Russian regions since July 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian intelligence officers, posing as girls, used the Telegram dating service 'Daivinchik' to befriend young Russian men ... Since July 2025, 46 young users of 'Daivinchik' have been detained in 16 Russian regions.

stories.headline: Ukraine hits two big Russian refineries as US Senate advances Russia sanctions bill 86-12

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian forces struck two of Russia's biggest oil refineries overnight into Wednesday, starting fires at a Lukoil refinery in the Perm region more than 1,500 km from Ukraine and at a refinery in Ryazan, Ukraine's Security Service and General Staff said.
key_facts.excerpt: The overnight attacks started fires at a Lukoil refinery in Russia's Perm region, more than 1,500 kilometers (900 miles) from Ukraine, and a refinery in Ryazan, about 400 kilometers (180 miles) from the border.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine says the two refineries have a combined annual capacity of around 220 million barrels; Ryazan Gov. Pavel Malkov said six people were hospitalised and drone debris caused fires at unidentified 'industrial sites'.
key_facts.excerpt: The refineries have a combined annual production capacity of around 220 million barrels of oil, according to Ukraine ... Ryazan Gov. Pavel Malkov said only that six people were taken to hospital after a drone attack.

key_facts.fact: Russian online retailer Wildberries, which Ukraine has targeted repeatedly in recent days, said it evacuated employees from a facility in Ryazan.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian online retailer Wildberries, a major supplier likened to Amazon that Ukraine has targeted in recent days, said it evacuated employees from a facility in Ryazan.

key_facts.fact: The strikes came hours after Zelensky met Trump at the White House on Tuesday and met more than 60 US senators, plus representatives of Lockheed Martin, as Kyiv pushes for Patriot production licences and more sanctions.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy said he also had a meeting in Washington with representatives of both parties in the U.S. Senate, with more than 60 senators in attendance ... He also met with representatives of Lockheed Martin.

key_facts.fact: On July 28 the US Senate voted 86-12 to advance the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, with Zelensky watching from the chamber after a closed-door appeal to senators.
key_facts.excerpt: voting 86-12 on July 28 to advance sweeping legislation ... came immediately after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made a personal appeal to senators behind closed doors before watching the vote from the Senate chamber.

key_facts.fact: The bill would authorise tariffs of up to 200% on the largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, expand sanctions on Russian banks, oligarchs and the 'shadow fleet', and extend Iran sanctions through 2031; it still needs final Senate passage and House action after the August recess.
key_facts.excerpt: authorizes Trump to impose tariffs of up to 200 percent on the world's largest purchasers of Russian oil and natural gas ... It also extends sanctions on Iran through 2031.

sources.title: Ukraine claims major Russian oil refinery hit, hours after Zelenskyy, Trump meeting
U.S. Senate Advances Sweeping Russia Sanctions Bill in 86-12 Vote

stories.headline: Keiko Fujimori sworn in as Peru's president, the country's ninth leader in a decade

key_facts.fact: Conservative leader Keiko Fujimori was sworn in as Peru's president on Tuesday, July 28, after winning June's runoff by fewer than 50,000 votes.
key_facts.excerpt: Conservative leader Keiko Fujimori was sworn in as Peru's president on Tuesday after winning the June presidential runoff by a margin of fewer than 50,000 votes.

key_facts.fact: The 51-year-old, a four-time presidential candidate and daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, becomes the country's ninth president in a decade; only three Peruvian presidents in that period were elected by popular vote.
key_facts.excerpt: officially takes office as the country's ninth president in a decade ... Over the past decade, only three of Peru's presidents have been elected by popular vote.

key_facts.fact: In her inaugural address she announced a 15% increase in the minimum wage, a reorganisation of social services to fight rural malnutrition, and said the military will 'temporarily' lead security operations in crime-hit areas.
key_facts.excerpt: She also said on Tuesday she would reorganize social services to fight malnutrition in rural communities and announced a 15% increase in the nation's minimum wage. Fujimori said that the nation's military will 'temporarily' lead security operations in crime afflicted areas.

key_facts.fact: Fujimori campaigned on an 'iron fist' security policy modelled on El Salvador's Nayib Bukele, including building a megaprison modelled on the Cecot penitentiary.
key_facts.excerpt: Keiko Fujimori pledged to fight crime with an 'iron fist,' implementing some policies adopted by Salvadorean President Nayib Bukele, and also build a megaprison modeled after the notorious Cecot penitentiary in El Salvador.

key_facts.fact: Her Popular Force party and ally Popular Renovation will hold half the senate seats once the new legislature is installed, making removal by congress harder.
key_facts.excerpt: Fujimori's Popular Force party and its main ally, Popular Renovation, will hold half the senate seats once the new legislature is installed, making it harder for opposing legislators to attempt to remove her as president.

sources.title: Keiko Fujimori is inaugurated as Peru's president following a narrow election victory

stories.headline: Altimmune's GLP-1 drug cuts heavy drinking in Phase 2 alcohol use disorder trial

key_facts.fact: Altimmune announced on July 28 positive topline results from the RECLAIM Phase 2 trial of pemvidutide, a glucagon/GLP-1 dual receptor agonist, in patients with moderate to severe alcohol use disorder.
key_facts.excerpt: GAITHERSBURG, Md., July 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Altimmune, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALT) ... today announced positive topline results from the RECLAIM Phase 2 trial evaluating pemvidutide.

key_facts.fact: The trial met its primary endpoint: heavy drinking days per week fell 4.20 from baseline at week 24 on pemvidutide versus 2.75 on placebo, a difference of 1.45 days (p=0.0014).
key_facts.excerpt: Change from baseline in HDD/Week at Week 24 (Primary Endpoint) -2.75 (LS mean) -4.20 (LS mean) -1.45 (LS mean difference) 0.0014

key_facts.fact: 64.4% of treated patients (29 of 45) achieved a two-level reduction in WHO Risk Drinking Levels versus 34.8% on placebo (p=0.0049), and 42.2% recorded zero heavy drinking days in weeks 21-24 versus 17.4% (p=0.0066).
key_facts.excerpt: 2-level Reduction in WHO-RDL 34.8% (16/46) 64.4% (29/45) Odds Ratio 3.31 0.0049 Zero HDD in Week 21 through Week 24 17.4% (8/46) 42.2% (19/45)

key_facts.fact: Patients on the drug also lost weight, with a placebo-adjusted reduction of 9.1% at 24 weeks (p<0.0001) and no sign of plateauing.
key_facts.excerpt: Statistically significant reduction in body weight, as measured by a placebo-adjusted difference in change from baseline of 9.1% at 24 weeks (p<0.0001), with no evidence of plateauing

key_facts.fact: Side effects were mostly gastrointestinal — nausea in 44% of treated patients versus 24% on placebo — and 10% discontinued because of drug-related adverse events versus 0% on placebo; the company plans to request an end-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA.
key_facts.excerpt: Nausea 12 (24%) 22 (44%) ... Study drug-related AEs leading to treatment discontinuation 0 (0%) 5 (10%) ... The Company plans to request an End-of-Phase 2 meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

sources.title: Altimmune Announces Positive Topline Results from RECLAIM Phase 2 Trial of Pemvidutide in Alcohol Use Disorder

stories.headline: Katalyst's spacecraft spins out of control, threatening rescue of NASA's Swift telescope

key_facts.fact: In a July 28 update, Katalyst Space Technologies said its Link spacecraft had been in a 'multi-axis spin' for the previous 72 hours because of attitude control problems that caused a temporary loss of communications and a bus reset.
key_facts.excerpt: In a July 28 update posted on social media, Katalyst Space Technologies said its Link spacecraft, launched July 3, was in a 'multi-axis spin' caused by attitude control issues that also affected spacecraft communications.

key_facts.fact: Two of Link's three reaction wheels are not working and its reaction control system thrusters are only partially working.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said that two of the three reaction wheels on Link, used for attitude control, were not functioning and that the spacecraft's reaction control system thrusters were only partially working.

key_facts.fact: Link launched July 3 on a Pegasus XL to rendezvous and dock with NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, a gamma-ray telescope in a decaying orbit that would reenter late this year or early next year without intervention.
key_facts.excerpt: Link launched into low Earth orbit on a Pegasus XL on a mission to rendezvous and dock with NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory ... in a decaying orbit and will reenter late this year or early next year without intervention.

key_facts.fact: NASA awarded Katalyst Space a $30 million contract last September for the reboost attempt.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA awarded Katalyst Space a $30 million contract last September to attempt a reboost mission.

key_facts.fact: The company says communications, propulsion and the robotics needed to grapple Swift are working, and it is using gimbaled electric thrusters to reduce the spin before updating guidance software and approaching Swift.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Over the coming days, Katalyst will work to reduce the body rates using the gimbaled electric propulsion thrusters and stabilize the spacecraft. We have already begun this series of burns and are seeing the intended effect.'

sources.title: Swift reboost mission encounters attitude control problems
